context: The undirected graph on the left has five vertices, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, and seven undirected edges: 1—3, 1—5, 3—2, 2—5, 2—4, 5—4, and 1—2.
description: In the adjacency list on the right, the left column is labeled “Vertex.” Its five green head nodes are 1, 3, 2, 5, and 4 from top to bottom. A green linked list extends to the right in each row under the label “All vertices connected to this vertex.” The table follows the row order in the figure.

Right-pointing arrows within a row represent linked-list references. They do not give the edges of the original graph a direction. Two neighbors listed consecutively in a row need not be connected to each other in the graph. Each undirected edge appears once in each endpoint's list, giving 14 adjacency nodes in addition to the five head nodes in the left column.

frames.explanation: For example, edge 1—2 appears as 2 in the list for vertex 1 and as 1 in the list for vertex 2. Vertices 1 and 4 have no edge between them, so neither appears in the other's list.
frames.title: Adjacency list representation of a graph

summary: A linked list of neighbors for each vertex represents the connections in the original graph.
